newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia energy minister tenders resignation.
newsitem.headline: Russia energy minister tenders resignation.

text.p: Russian Fuel and Energy Minister Pyotr Rodionov has tendered his resignation, a ministry spokesman said on Friday.

Spokesman Sergei Slesaryev could not comment on the reasons for Rodionov's decision to quit the government, but he said the government press service would release a statement soon. Rodionov was appointed minister in August 1996.
Rodionov was previously director of Lentransgaz, a regional transportation unit of Russia's natural gas monopoly Gazprom.
He was overseeing a sector of the economy still struggling to reverse a long slump in output -- Russian gas production is flat but oil output has been falling for a decade.

Oil output was 6.03 million barrels per day last year, down from a 1987 peak of 11.39 million barrels per day. Russia, once the world's biggest oil producer, now ranks behind Saudi Arabia and the United States.

Analysts say the energy sector could hold the key to Russian economic revival. GDP has been contracting since the collapse of the Soviet Union in 1991, although International Monetary Fund Managing Director Michel Camdessus said on Thursday that growth could start this year.
